fight: Does the ensemble-vs-GP surrogate-class ranking depend on ensemble size K, or is it robust to K?

side_a.position: The surrogate-class ranking FLIPS with K: at K=2 the ensemble's task-normalized marginal (0.95) EXCEEDS the exact GP's (0.846); the field-standard K=5 is where the ensemble is weakest (0.52→0.32→0.18 at K=3/5/10).
claims: our K-sweep: ensemble marginal 0.95/0.52/0.32/0.18 at K=2/3/5/10

side_b.position: Ensemble size is NOT a decisive hyperparameter for the surrogate comparison: rankings are robust to it.
claims: "the different ensembles perform similarly across many experiments, showing the robustness of our results to this hyperparameter" (Fig A.7)

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical. L/R/W ablate K=5-vs-10 (never tested K=2, where our flip occurs); our sweep includes K=2. Scope-limited disagreement — the flip may live in the small-K regime L/R/W did not probe.
scope_overlap: genuine disagreement at the claim level, but possibly reconcilable: L/R/W's 'robustness' is over K∈{5,10}; our flip is driven by K=2. This SHARPENS N2 (nobody reports a ranking flip) while ARMING a reviewer who cites L/R/W's robustness claim.

fight: Is the ensemble's jagged posterior mean an intrinsic surrogate-CLASS property (mechanism), or a finite-width / under-training / low-K artifact (taxonomy)?

side_a.position: Prior-task smoothness match is the surrogate-class axis governing the GP-ensemble gap (candidate C's thesis).
claims: the GP wins because its posterior mean is smooth; smoothing the ensemble should close the gap (M1)

side_b.position: Jaggedness is a finite-width/capacity artifact, not a class property: infinite-width nets ARE Gaussian processes and finite nets are spectrally biased toward low-frequency (smooth) functions; our own K=2≫K=5 result is capacity evidence.
claims: infinite-width nets converge to a GP/NTK
finite nets exhibit spectral bias toward smooth functions
K=2 ensemble beats K=5 → capacity/averaging, not class geometry

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is theoretically stronger (NTK/GP equivalence is a theorem; spectral bias is broadly replicated) and is corroborated by our OWN K-sweep. Side A currently rests on unmanipulated correlation (M1/M2 not yet run per MECHANISM_EXPERIMENTS.md).
scope_overlap: Genuine and internal: the same evidence (K-sweep) that makes N2 novel also undercuts C's mechanism framing and supports D's taxonomy framing. The draft must engage this as the central self-inflicted risk (N5).

fight: Does the GP win because its posterior VARIANCE grows away from data (σ-mediated, LCB as implicit trust region), or is σ largely irrelevant to the gap?

side_a.position: Distance-aware variance growth is real and standard nets/ensembles lack it — the GP's growing σ makes LCB an implicit trust region (the N4 hypothesis-at-risk).
claims: GP-RBF variance 'increases monotonically toward 1 as x* moves further away'
ensembles 'assign low uncertainty to OOD examples even if far from the data'

side_b.position: σ is NOT the mediator: removing the σ term (β=0) barely moves the gap (0.51→0.47); and a GP does not automatically get variance growth (needs bi-Lipschitz features); TuRBO uses Thompson (not LCB) and treats unchecked variance growth as a problem.
claims: β=0 control: gap 0.51→0.47
unconstrained deep-kernel GP is 'certain even far away from the training data' (DUE)
TuRBO: 0 LCB hits; explicit TR counters variance-driven over-exploration

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has our own β=0 control + DUE's counterexample; Side A has the established distance-aware-uncertainty mechanism but no offline-MBO/LCB tie. Note the β=0 control 'has no generator in the codebase and is being recomputed' — evidence quality on side B is provisional.
scope_overlap: Partly genuine, partly scoped: SNGP owns the general mechanism; the offline-MBO 'LCB + growing variance = implicit trust region' synthesis is NONE FOUND. Resolution shapes N4 verdict and whether C's mechanism survives on the σ side.

fight: Does the optimizer / search strategy matter in offline MBO (PGS premise), or is it near-irrelevant (our η²_opt=0.01)?

side_a.position: Offline BBO has focused on surrogates while using fixed search strategies; the SEARCH strategy is the neglected, decisive axis.
claims: PGS premise: search strategy is the neglected axis worth improving

side_b.position: The optimizer main effect is 0.01 — the field has been innovating on the axis that does not matter.
claims: η²_optimizer = 0.01 vs η²_surrogate = 0.37/0.405

evidence_quality_delta: Side B's η²_opt=0.01 is itself confounded per FLAW_LEDGER P0-0/P0-1 (unequal oracle budgets; a trust region closes the gradient collapse 15× on Branin) — so the reversal is 'currently unearned' until X1/X3 re-run. A three-way tension: PGS says optimizer matters; our raw number says it doesn't; our own audit says the number isn't yet identified.
scope_overlap: Genuine — and it is the paper's rhetorical 'named belief, refuted' hook. Directly relevant to whether A/D can claim the reversal.

fight: When you de-confound a benchmarked comparison, does the headline effect SHRINK (reality-check norm) or can it GROW?

side_a.position: Auditing/de-confounding SHRINKS or vanishes the effect — the reality-check genre norm.
claims: tuned LSTMs overturn newer SOTA; 'effect sizes tend to be much smaller' (Melis)
DML gains 'marginal at best' once controlled (Musgrave)
6/7 neural recommenders lose to simple baselines (Ferrari Dacrema)
GANs: 'no algorithm clearly dominates' (Lucic)

side_b.position: De-confounding can GROW the effect: fixing target-scaling + candidate-protocol nets η²_surr UP from 0.37 to 0.405.
claims: η²_surr 0.367→0.405 after fixing confounds (i)+(ii)
Recht: 'increased advantage over earlier models' (relative slope >1)
Bressan: stricter spec 'came out stronger'

evidence_quality_delta: Side A is the dominant, well-replicated genre pattern; Side B has our result + two PARTIAL precedents (Recht = relative not absolute; Bressan = psychology, no effect-size stat). No ML/CS paper shows an audited headline exceeding its published value.
scope_overlap: Genuine genre-level tension. This is N9: the de-confounding DIRECTION is the rhetorical asset if it is unclaimed within ML/CS (it appears to be).

fight: Are deep-ensemble advantages a genuine class benefit or a capacity effect a single larger model reproduces?

side_a.position: Deep ensembles give simple, scalable predictive-uncertainty and accuracy gains.
claims: ensembles give well-calibrated uncertainty; recommend M=5 members

side_b.position: Ensemble gains are largely a capacity effect that a single larger model reproduces.
claims: a single larger model matches ensemble accuracy gains

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical; Abe is the more recent, targeted test. Neither ties to a surrogate-CLASS RANKING in BO/offline-MBO — so both stop short of N2.
scope_overlap: Scoped: about ensemble-vs-single-net accuracy, not ensemble-vs-GP ranking. Supports the 'K/capacity is the confound' reading (N5) without owning N2.
